cause: Context Pack was frozen before development started.
impact: The line has an evidence-bound starting context.
lesson: Freeze the initial context before changing implementation state.

cause: The classification adapter, metric and explanation modules were intentionally absent when the new known-answer contract tests were first collected.
impact: The focused suite failed during collection with a missing classification adapter module before any implementation code was added.
lesson: Freeze known-answer adapter, metric and explanation contracts before implementing the model family seam.

cause: New classification consumer tests were added before implementation.
impact: The focused consumer suite fails at import because the typed classification projection seam is not implemented yet.
lesson: Keep consumer contracts red before implementation and prove the packet-backed boundary with focused tests.

cause: The protocol boundary tests were added before the sealed-holdout orchestration module existed.
impact: The classification consumer suite fails during collection with a missing classification_protocol module.
lesson: Define the holdout seal and protocol orchestration as a typed seam before exposing the result to consumers.

cause: The new classification tests first referenced absent typed contracts, the safe split manifest builder, and the fold-local classification preprocessor.
impact: No production implementation was accepted before the tests demonstrated the missing capability boundary.
lesson: Keep classification contract and leakage tests red before adding the implementation surface.

cause: Mutation-style edge tests exposed a datetime interval arithmetic assumption, missing-column misclassification, and empty decision costs being treated as invalid instead of unknown scenarios.
impact: The first implementation was not accepted until these typed fail-closed edge cases were corrected and rerun.
lesson: Exercise date-like intervals, missing columns, and unknown policy inputs explicitly before declaring the typed core green.

cause: The typed classification contracts, explicit IID/group/temporal/panel split manifest, and fold-local preprocessing contract passed their focused and legacy regression gates.
impact: The package-local classification core is green for this bounded test surface; integration, provider, browser, and release gates remain separate.
lesson: Keep the classification focused gate separate from central integration and release acceptance.

cause: The v1.8.6 prediction boundary regression imports artifacts before a pre-existing dirty predictive_research __init__.py; that unrelated package export imports consumer_projection and creates an artifacts circular import.
impact: The bounded classification and old kernel gates remain valid, but the old prediction boundary is not current-worktree-verified until the unrelated dirty package export is resolved by its owner.
lesson: Separate an out-of-scope dirty baseline import failure from the classification kernel gate and do not alter unowned files to force green.

cause: The package-wide classification regression was run while the separate first worker was still writing shared classification protocol and leakage-test files; the observed failures were an intermediate OOF assertion and then a duplicate keyword syntax error in that sibling scope.
impact: The four-file adapter, metrics and explanations focused gate remains independently green; the sibling package-wide gate cannot be treated as final until its writer publishes stable files.
lesson: Run cross-line regression only after each parallel writer has reached a stable syntax and protocol checkpoint; keep its intermediate failures separate from the non-overlapping seam gate.

cause: The package-local review checked immutable identity receipts, strict availability and label interval predicates, explicit embargo basis, no legacy random fallback, fold-local row refs and unsafe feature-type rejection.
impact: The review found no remaining defect inside the five requested write paths; central integration and release claims remain unverified.
lesson: Review safety predicates and evidence boundaries separately from model-family expansion and central cutover.

cause: The requested five-file classification contracts, safe split and fold-local preprocessing line passed its final bounded test and process checks.

evidence.ref: 33 classification tests; 13 v1.8.6 split/preprocessing/contract regressions; 46 passed; compileall; git diff --check; devline verify

impact: The non-overlapping typed classification core is green within its declared file boundary. P0 C1 integration, real host, Agent/Notebook/Report cutover, provider, browser and release acceptance remain unverified.
lesson: Close a package-local write gate with exact tests and preserve all deferred integration boundaries as explicit not verified claims.

cause: The new package exports eagerly imported artifact-backed consumer helpers while workbench.artifacts was still importing the schema registry.
impact: The full predictive-research collection failed for two existing v1.8.6 tests before any test body ran.
lesson: Artifact-backed extensions must be lazy package exports so the existing artifact module remains acyclic.

cause: The fold-local preprocessing numeric helper returned a RangeIndex series and pandas aligned it against server row IDs during assignment.
impact: A non-default row identity produced silent NaNs in transformed features and blocked protocol execution.
lesson: Information-set row identity must be preserved through every pandas transform; add a non-default-index regression probe.

cause: The second classification ML seam implements typed Logistic Regression and Random Forest adapters, bounded metrics, validation-only permutation explanations and known-answer contracts within its four allowed write paths.
impact: The focused seam and legacy prediction/control regression evidence is green; sibling first-worker package-wide acceptance, central cutover, provider, browser and release evidence remain separate.
lesson: Keep model-family expansion behind one typed adapter seam and preserve metric denominators, undefined reasons, validation scope and class order as evidence fields.

cause: Review covered explicit adapter parameters and bounds, deterministic class/probability ordering, weight validation, unknown-model refusal, weighted denominators, undefined metric reasons, calibration and threshold scopes, validation-only permutation inputs, stability and support labels, and non-causal explanation metadata.
impact: No remaining defect was found inside the four requested write paths for the package-local seam. Real provider/catalog discovery, central cutover, browser, release and sibling first-worker final acceptance are not verified by this review.
lesson: A green seam review is not an integration claim; preserve the later protocol, evidence consumer and host/provider gates as separate acceptance boundaries.

cause: The first protocol version treated a non-empty cost matrix and capacity as sufficient for threshold selection but delegated selection to max_f1 without applying the declared policy semantics.
impact: A selected threshold could be reported even when cost and capacity were not used, weakening decision correctness and evidence trust.
lesson: Decision policy fields must either affect the typed selection algorithm or fail closed; cost/utility and capacity semantics must be recorded in the threshold receipt.

cause: The first multiclass protocol path called the metric bundle without an explicit macro or weighted averaging policy.
impact: The typed metric contract correctly rejected the ambiguous multiclass evaluation instead of silently selecting an averaging convention.
lesson: Multiclass metrics must carry an explicit averaging policy at every fold, OOF, holdout and baseline evaluation.

cause: The new expected-utility validation applied required cost keys to an empty cost mapping, although an empty mapping is the existing typed representation for unknown costs.
impact: An unknown-cost policy was rejected instead of remaining available as scenarios-only evidence.
lesson: Unknown policy inputs must retain their explicit scenarios-only state; only non-empty malformed declarations should fail closed.

cause: The first protocol packet declared a shuffle-target control but did not execute a target permutation through the shared fold-local adapter path.
impact: Consumers could not distinguish an executed negative control from a metadata receipt, weakening the model-evidence boundary.
lesson: A control is evidence only when it runs on the declared exchangeability unit, split manifest and development-only scope; unsupported temporal/panel units must be unavailable rather than row-shuffled.

cause: The temporal rolling split includes a development warm-up period without a validation fold, but the first protocol treated every development row as an OOF row.
impact: Temporal classification runs incorrectly failed as incomplete OOF instead of keeping warm-up rows in development refit only.
lesson: OOF evidence is exactly the development rows assigned to validation folds; warm-up and purged rows must never enter OOF metrics or threshold selection.

cause: The P1 worktree has no frontend node_modules and the root Vitest configuration resolves its setup file and cache outside the writable worktree; the renderer test could not be executed in the isolated worktree.
impact: TypeScript/Vitest renderer acceptance remains NOT VERIFIED; the component and test only passed esbuild syntax bundling.
lesson: Frontend package dependencies and an isolated test cache must be provisioned before claiming renderer or browser acceptance.

cause: An adversarial plan-to-code review found temporal future-row training, invalid known-entity panel acceptance, metric-direction inversion, post-computation holdout sealing, exploration results marked validated, and baseline class-order drift despite green focused tests.
impact: The P1 package cannot be closed or integrated until these correctness and evidence-boundary failures have regression tests and fixes.
lesson: Green package tests are not sufficient when they do not probe information order, metric direction, policy status, class-column identity, or actual holdout release ordering.

cause: The classification split manifest did not expose a forward-only training role for temporal validation folds and did not reject a panel_known_entity_future holdout entity absent from development.
impact: A downstream fold consumer could train on development rows after the validation period, or accept a new entity under the known-entity profile.
lesson: Ordered split manifests must materialize auditable historical training row refs per fold and enforce the entity-set contract before execution.

cause: The relevant classification protocol regression suite expects fit_probability_calibrator, but the current P1 classification_metrics module does not expose it.
impact: The split-only change passes its focused and legacy split tests, while the broader classification protocol regression remains red outside this task's two-file boundary.
lesson: Report split correctness separately from unrelated protocol implementation gaps; do not widen a scoped split fix to repair another package boundary.

cause: Moving baseline computation into the one-shot holdout release callback left packet assembly reading majority_label and baseline_probability_matrix from the old outer scope.
impact: All protocol consumers failed after the holdout seal refactor with NameError before producing a classification packet.
lesson: When evidence is moved behind a release capability, every downstream field must consume the released typed bundle rather than the pre-refactor lexical scope.

cause: The packet identity initially included dataset, task, and split only, so changing the candidate model or DecisionPolicy could reuse an evidence artifact identity even though the result changed.
impact: Artifact caches and downstream lineage could confuse model/policy revisions with the prior classification result.
lesson: Typed evidence identity must bind every decision-relevant input, not only the data and split snapshots.

cause: The full persistence and Graph subset reached the existing typed classification entrypoint, which fails in classification_metrics.py because development_calibration_eval is rejected as a calibrator transform scope.
impact: The existing typed entrypoint regression remains unverified for this subtask because it fails before persistence; the failure is outside the authorized files.
lesson: Keep persistence hardening evidence separate from unrelated classification protocol or metrics failures outside the authorized boundary.

cause: The full classification consumer suite fails in classification_protocol.py for two multiclass cases because the calibration branch raises on incomplete OOF probability refs before any persistence consumer runs.
impact: The full classification consumer suite is not green, but the two failures are outside the authorized persistence and Graph files.
lesson: Do not widen a persistence hardening change to repair an unrelated multiclass protocol calibration boundary.

cause: The authorized persistence and Graph regression gate passed after adding disk digest verification, idempotent file integrity checks and Graph conflict preflight.

evidence.ref: focused persistence/Graph pytest=4 passed; boundary pytest=4 passed; compileall; git diff --check; formal verify

impact: The authorized persistence hardening behavior is regression-covered; the full classification consumer suite retains two unrelated multiclass calibration failures recorded separately.
lesson: Close a narrow persistence gate with direct fail-closed probes while keeping unrelated protocol failures explicitly outside scope.

cause: A final rerun of the complete authorized classification consumer file passed all collected tests after the focused persistence hardening gate.
impact: The final local classification consumer regression is green; no protocol or metrics source was changed by this subtask.
lesson: When a broader existing-suite failure is not reproducible, retain its historical evidence and report the fresh rerun separately.

cause: The blocked consumer projection redacted evaluation, baseline, control, comparison, and explanation sections but still forwarded candidate models containing development metrics and selection scores.
impact: A blocked or exploration-only packet could still expose numeric model evidence through the models section, bypassing the intended fail-closed consumer boundary.
lesson: Fail-closed projections must audit every route by which formal numeric evidence can escape, including candidate lists and policy metadata.

cause: The first adversarial review identified holdout over-release, calibrator reuse, out-of-band temporal/entity keys, weighted-stage gaps, packet hash optionality, and persistence digest/concurrency gaps that focused tests did not cover.
impact: P1 could not be considered safe for integration until the evidence boundary and persistence boundary were made fail-closed.
lesson: Correctness review must probe the order and identity of real data consumption, not only the shape of a final packet; remaining browser, provider, and central cutover gates stay separate.

cause: The new metric evidence assertions initially failed because metric_definition, structured denominator, weighted status, and evidence_basis were absent.
impact: bounded to the metric evidence subtask; no protocol or persistence state changed
lesson: Write and observe evidence-semantic red tests before extending metric receipts.

cause: The full two-file classification suite retained three pre-existing diagnostics/import failures outside the metric evidence subtask.
impact: full classification suite remains non-green outside this bounded metric task; focused metric/oracle/sensitivity tests remain the acceptance scope
lesson: Keep out-of-scope protocol and diagnostics failures separate from focused metric evidence acceptance.

cause: The first diagnostics contribution did not expose the declared columns, support threshold, bins, statistics, or plan body as an immutable holdout-release contract.

evidence.ref: tests/predictive_research/test_classification_contracts_v189.py; tests/predictive_research/test_classification_protocol_v189.py; tests/predictive_research/test_classification_consumers_v189.py; 146 passed; compileall; git diff --check; devline verify

impact: A downstream consumer could not independently explain which subgroup and shift facts were authorized, and a mutable diagnostics plan could change the evidence identity after construction.
lesson: Holdout subgroup and shift evidence must be an exact, immutable, predeclared section with a self-contained plan and descriptive-only statistics.

cause: The package-local P1 classification capability reached its declared backend, persistence, provider contribution, renderer contribution, and process-control verification boundary.

evidence.ref: focused backend=146 passed; broader backend=222 passed, 2 skipped, 3 warnings; renderer=4 passed; typecheck; compileall; git diff --check; formal verify; generated retrospective

impact: The classification ML package can be handed to the later single-writer integration line with exact deferred boundaries instead of an unqualified release claim.
lesson: Record package-local correctness and UI contribution gates separately from central Agent/Notebook cutover, browser acceptance, external providers and release integration.
